summary: A narrator, communicating through encrypted messages with a contact called Wheeze, learns that their friend Wilson has been detained in connection with a terrorism investigation, and that Zip was detained too. The narrator, who had used a campus computer lab with limited surveillance, reflects on Wilson as a harmless, clumsy 'doofus' whose past trouble was minor, such as the gourmet pickle incident, and therefore finds the charge hard to believe. The narrator suspects Zip, an older take-charge figure who lives with Wheeze's family, of being a 'rat' and wonders whether the messages can be trusted.
one_line: A narrator learns through encrypted messages that friend Wilson has been detained in a terrorism investigation, and suspects Zip of betrayal.
key_facts: The narrator had used a campus computer lab once after forgetting a power cord and never went back there again.
The student worker told the narrator that the campus lacked budget to cover the whole campus, leaving a handful of spots surveillance-free, including that lab.
The narrator's messages to Wheeze used end-to-end encryption and an open source program that everyone on the Group vouched for.
The narrator checked the program's code line by line.
Wheeze messaged that Wilson was "detained in connection with a ter- rorism investigation."
Wilson was described as a friendly doofus whose biggest problem was that he wanted everyone to like him.
Wilson once had $600 worth of gourmet pickles explode across a fancy grocery store floor after bumping into a display while goofing off with friends.
The narrator said Wilson "wasn't smart enough" to be a terrorist and "wasn't a terrorist."
Wheeze wrote that Zip had also been detained.
The narrator typed "He's a rat" to Wheeze, first deleting a draft version before retyping it.
Zip had crashed on a couch at Wheeze's house after a protest and had been living there ever since.
Zip was older than Wilson and was a more take-charge kind of guy.
Everybody loved Zip, according to the narrator.
Wheeze was running through everything Zip had said and done, as the narrator had done weeks earlier.
